content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves the Isaiah 7:14 collision by balancing isolated verses and word-count evidence, so it does the thing K-C governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"Phrase: the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together. Readings weighed: it requires an explicit chain-vs-chain framing in the judge text, or it applies whenever the judge weighs a party's own chain witnesses against a link as this text does with C5's own narrowing and the sign's chapter bounds.","why":"K-C requires chain-against-chain weighing by footing when the pressed witnesses are the pressing side's own chain, and this text instead calls the link underdetermined because individual verses and word-count cut both ways."}
